problem: The sentence 'The indicator is a small generator or a drag-cup mechanism' mixes two different instruments and reads as if both are parts of the indicator. A drag-cup (eddy-current) tachometer has a shaft-driven rotating magnet that drags a spring-restrained metal cup; no generator sits in the indicator.
fix: Two common direct types are used. In one, the shaft drives a small generator whose voltage moves a voltmeter. In the other, the shaft drives a rotating magnet that drags a spring-restrained metal cup (drag-cup or eddy-current tachometer). Both are direct and need no aircraft power supply, but the long shaft adds friction, lag and a path for oil leaks.

problem: S is presented as a fixed 41 µV/°C for type K, but the Seebeck coefficient of type K changes with temperature (about 39 µV/°C near 0 °C and over 42 µV/°C in the middle of the range), so the linear formula is an approximation.
fix: Add one sentence: S = 41 µV/°C is an average value over the engine range; the real curve is slightly nonlinear and the indicator uses a lineariser or a lookup table. The linear formula is accurate enough for exam calculations.

problem: The compensation term 'S × T_cold' is only correct when the reference is 0 °C; a student may think any cold-junction temperature simply gets added as an absolute figure.
fix: Say: cold-junction compensation adds the emf the couple would give if its cold junction were at the 0 °C reference, that is S × T_cold, so the total becomes S × (T_hot − T_cold) + S × T_cold = S × T_hot.

problem: The node note 'about 41 µV/°C' is the sensitivity of the sensor, not the size of the millivolt signal, which is about 41 µV per degree of temperature difference (a few millivolts for hundreds of degrees). A student can misread the signal level.
fix: Change the note to 'few mV for hundreds of °C' and keep S = 41 µV/°C in the thermocouple node or the text.

problem: The caption says 'Both signals are conditioned', but the upper (speed) chain goes straight from 'Voltage or frequency' to the cockpit indicator with no conditioning block, while only the EGT chain shows 'Amplifier and ADC'.
fix: Either add a 'Signal conditioning' block (pulse counter or A/D) between 'Voltage or frequency' and 'Cockpit indicator', or reword the caption to 'The EGT signal is amplified and digitised; both signals meet at one cockpit indicator.'

problem: Only two spools are defined; on three-spool engines there is also N3, and a student meeting N3 in another text has no anchor.
fix: Add: three-spool engines add N3 for the intermediate-pressure spool; the same percent-of-reference rule applies.

problem: 'A slow EGT drift at the same N1 can show a dirty compressor or a drifting sensor' omits that EGT also moves with ambient temperature, altitude and bleed configuration, so drift must be judged against a comparable baseline.
fix: Say: a slow EGT drift at the same N1, altitude and air temperature (compared with the engine's recorded baseline) can show a dirty compressor or a drifting sensor.
